meta.title: About — Crucible
meta.description: What Crucible is, why it exists, and where it's going.

hero.headline: Don't compete. Complete.
hero.subheadline: Crucible builds open-source tools that make coding harnesses work better. Forge distributes shared context. Ember reconstructs session trees and groups agent work across harnesses. Each product integrates with the tools and backends developers already use.

metaphor.heading: The metallurgy metaphor
metaphor.description: A crucible is the vessel where raw materials are refined under pressure into something useful. Every product name maps to a stage in the metalworking process.

items.name: Forge
items.description: — Shape raw materials into useful tools (CLI that shapes configs)

items.name: Smelt
items.description: — Extract pure metal from ore (shared plugin engine library)

items.name: Anvil
items.description: — The surface you build on (SDK for third-party plugins)

items.name: Lathe
items.description: — Precision shaping tool (MCP server wrapping forge commands)

items.name: Foundry
items.description: — Where you cast finished goods (plugin registry/marketplace)

items.name: Ember
items.description: — The glow that shows where heat is (agent observability)

items.title: Don't compete, complete
items.description: Build the cross-harness coordination layer that no single vendor will build. Complement every tool, compete with none.

items.title: DX is the whole product
items.description: If it's not delightful to use, it doesn't ship. Developer experience isn't a feature — it's the product itself.

items.title: Build for the final vision from day one
items.description: Architecture supports the endgame even when shipping an MVP. No throwaway scaffolding.

items.title: Speed over completeness
items.description: Ship narrow, iterate fast. A working tool today beats a perfect tool next quarter.

items.title: Community is the moat
items.description: Open source. MIT license. Community contributions outscale any solo effort.

items.title: Cross-tool is the structural advantage
items.description: No harness vendor will solve the multi-harness problem. The value is in the space between tools.

items.title: Platform outlasts any individual tool
items.description: Coding harnesses will come and go. The coordination infrastructure persists.

roadmap.heading: Product roadmap
roadmap.footer: Architecture: focused CLIs, with shared infrastructure where products need it. See {link}.
roadmap.diagramAlt: Crucible product phases — shipped Forge milestones, Ember in development, and future Forge plugin and compiler milestones

architecture.heading: Path C: focused tools, shared infrastructure
architecture.description: Crucible is a platform of focused CLIs rather than a universal CLI. TypeScript and Bun power Forge and the planned plugin-based products. Ember is the exception: Go and the OpenTelemetry Collector fit its telemetry pipeline.
architecture.diagramAlt: Crucible ecosystem — focused tools for coding harnesses
architecture.caption: Each product is useful alone. Shared code, files, and open protocols connect them without replacing coding harnesses or observability backends.
